reason: The hypothesis relies on premises about HEA incorporation and interfacial bonding from Mg- and Al-based composites (E1, E3) and on benefits of uniform reinforcement distribution in W-based materials (E2). However, none of the cited evidence involves W-Cu composites, HEA reinforcement in W-Cu, or thermal conductivity measurements. The extrapolation from mechanical properties and thermal load capacity to improved thermal conductivity via reduced phase separation is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: HEA reinforcement can be incorporated into a metal matrix composite with uniform particle distribution and limited interfacial reaction
HEA reinforcement improves interfacial bonding and reduces porosity in metal matrix composites
Uniformly distributed reinforcement particles in a W-based composite enhance thermal load capacity and irradiation resistance
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced porosity from HEA addition will reduce phase separation and interfacial void formation in W-Cu
Reducing phase separation and interfacial voids will improve thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite
